newsitem.title: UK: OFTEL to look more closely at BT's global plans.
newsitem.headline: OFTEL to look more closely at BT's global plans.

text.p: Britain's telecommunications watchdog Oftel said on Thursday it was looking more closely at the global plans of once-monopoly British Telecommunications plc with a view of possibly amending BT's licensing obligations.

Oftel said it had prepared a consultative document designed to examine whether any change is "needed to BT's licence so that UK customers can continue to be assured of a good deal for telecommunications services, matching up to the best available in the world".
It noted that BT's proposed merger with MCI has highlighted the issue since it was only one of BT's 80-plus overseas investments.

"It is possible, however, that BT's moves towards globalisation may have an impact on the company's ability and willingness to meet its UK licence obligations," OFTEL Director General Don Cruickshank said.
Cruickshank said he was inviting comment on whether he should continue to rely on existing regulatory arrangements to secure the interests of consumers or amend the regulations.
The consultation document offers five options:
- OFTEL would continue to monitor closely the company's performance in meeting its obligations under the terms of the current license.
- OFTEL would modify the licence to impose a general prohibition on the company taking any action which could prejudice its ability to meet its service obligations in the UK.
- The above modification with an added requirement for annual review by the BT directors and certification by the auditors that the general prohibition was being complied with.

- OFTEL would impose an all-embracing duty on the company to secure the UK network business including securing that it had adequate management and financial resources, supported by detailed annual certification by directors and auditors.
